conviction_note: Small negative lean: a direct counterparty (Emirates, 5 Nov) shows the Gulf disruption that CAE blamed for two-thirds of its Q1 civil margin drop was still there through September, while consensus (C$0.27) asks for +17% YoY adjusted EPS after a flat Q1. The stock ran +17% in 20 sessions into a print, and its last six prints all closed flat or down on day one. The Flightscape capital-return angle is the main offset. Nothing decisive and unpriced was found, so p_up is 43 on a 6% scale (-0.84). The findings sum to -1.6 and are not fitted to that number.
bar: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) adjusted EPS C$0.27 on revenue C$1.256B (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CAE.CA/estimates). Earnings Whispers has US$0.19 on US$907.7M, whisper US$0.21 (https://finviz.com/news/414815/caes-defense-momentum-faces-a-civil-margin-test-as-middle-east-drag-lingers, 2026-11-03), about C$0.26-0.27 at ~0.72, so two sources roughly agree. Prior-year Q2 FY26 was adj EPS C$0.23 on C$1.236B. Q1 FY27 was C$0.26, flat YoY. The company's own guide is FY27 adjusted EPS C$1.21-1.28, reaffirmed 2026-08-12 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001173382/000117338226000040/cae_q1fy27xex1xpressrelease.htm). FY consensus sits at the bottom of that range (US$0.87, about C$1.21). The May release said the guide assumed the Middle East war ends before October (https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/2026/05/22/iran-war-hammers-caes-bottom-line-with-training-centre-shutdowns-on-the-horizon/).
positioning_check: US short interest about 5.56M shares and 7.2 days to cover on US volume, ShortSqueeze, as of 2026-08-29 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=CAE). Curved Trading had 5.6M and 8.2 days at the 2026-08-14 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cae/short-interest/). That is under 2% of roughly 320M shares, not crowded; days to cover look high only because most turnover is on the TSX. No October settlement was found. The skew is unavailable: the US option chain is unusable (OI 28, ATM spread 100% of mid). Tape: 20d run-up +16.6% (23.24 on 10-14 to 27.73 on 11-10, a steady climb plus +4.3% on the Flightscape sale day); 52w high -20%. Bullish sentiment 30.4% against 25.0% a quarter earlier, per the Earnings Whispers preview.

findings.finding: Emirates Group's half-year (Apr-Sep 2026) results, published 2026-11-05, i.e. after CAE last spoke on 08-12, describe 'the ongoing conflict in the Gulf region' with 'intermittent airspace restrictions and closures'. Passengers fell 22-25%, ASKs -17%, the network stood at only 91% of pre-disruption by 30 Sep, and headcount was down 2%. CAE said about two-thirds of its Q1 civil margin decline (20.2% to 16.5%) came from the Middle East, including its JVs there. It said the drag would take 'another quarter or two to subside', and its FY27 guide (C$1.21-1.28, consensus at the bottom) assumed the war ends before October. That makes a Q2 drag at least as large as Q1's likely, and puts the H2 assumption at risk: a trimmed guide, or one held only with a lower H2 civil margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide/outlook was the line on two of the last three prints. May 2026: FY27 framed as a 'reset year', adj EPS in line, stock -14.0% (26.94 to 23.16). Feb 2026: civil outlook lowered, offset by defense, -3.7%. Aug 2026: outlook unchanged, 'aligned with plans', -4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Emirates numbers are a Gulf-airline headline, and no CAE preview found links them to CAE's Middle East JVs or to the guide's 'war ends before October' assumption. The Earnings Whispers preview of 11-03 predates them and calls consensus at the bottom of the guide conservative. If the market had priced a guide cut, the stock would not have climbed +17% into the print to within 1% of its post-August high. Against that: management already told the market to expect one or two more quarters of drag, so the Q2 part is inside guidance. This is sized as a risk to the outlook, not as a quarter miss.
findings.independence: The same picture comes from CAE's own Q1 call transcript ('Middle East effects, which will take another quarter or two to subside... we don't see incremental risk in the year', https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CAE/Q12027), which argues partly against the guidance risk. Proxy: Emirates is a counterparty in the region, not CAE's own number.

findings.finding: Consensus arithmetic, an inference from company documents: the Q2 bar of C$0.27 is +17% on Q2 FY26's C$0.23, while Q1 FY27 printed flat at C$0.26. Q1 adjusted segment operating income was 156.6M (civil 106.1 plus defense 50.5), down about 7.5% from Q1 FY26's about 169M. Q2 FY26's base was 155.3M (civil 16.2% margin, defense 8.2%), and seasonality cut civil margin about 4 points from Q1 to Q2 last year (20.2% to 16.2%). Reaching C$0.27 needs Q2 SOI up about 8-10% YoY, with civil margin holding near Q1's 16.5% through its weak season while bid and proposal costs stay elevated and the government R&D benefit is gone. Defense at about 9.5-10% on about C$580M gives about +10M YoY; civil would need about +3% more.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not bought much. Nov 2025: adj EPS beat by about 15% and revenue by about 9%, +5.8% after hours, closed +0.04% (27.42 to 27.43). Feb 2026: beat Zacks, -3.7%. May 2026: in line, -14%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews quote the C$0.27 / US$0.19 bar with no segment walk. If the street had modelled Q2 civil seasonality on top of the Middle East drag, the Q2 bar would sit near the prior year's C$0.23-0.25, not at +17%.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 segment figures come from a separate document: https://www.cae.com/content/docs/FY26_Second_quarter_financial_report_EN.pdf (2025-11-11). Consensus comes from Chartmill (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CAE.CA/estimates). Counter-evidence: in Q1, below-SOI items (interest, share count, tax) offset a -7.5% SOI drop, and the same support may lift Q2. Inference, not a company number for Q2.

findings.finding: CAE agreed on 2026-10-26 to sell Flightscape to SITA for US$500M EV and said the proceeds go to its core businesses and to 'returning capital to shareholders'. On the Q1 call the chair said a dividend had not been decided ('We haven't made any decision on that'), and CAE bought back 1.1M shares (C$39M) under its NCIB in Q1. The Q2 release or call is the first chance to set out a capital-return plan: a larger NCIB, a dividend reinstatement or an SIB.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior capital-return announcement at a print was found. The stock rose +4.3% on the sale announcement (25.00 to 26.09, 2026-10-26).
findings.why_not_priced: The sale itself is priced: the stock rose 4.3% that day and kept climbing. A specific return of capital has not been announced. Closing is not expected until H1 2027, so management may defer the details, which is why this is small. If a return were expected, it would show up in previews; none mention one.
findings.independence: Dividend comments from the Q1 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CAE/Q12027). Deal terms confirmed by BNN Bloomberg (https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/company-news/2026/10/26/cae-to-sell-aviation-operations-software-business-flightscape/).

findings.finding: The reaction history, rebuilt from confirmed results releases (Yahoo daily closes, close before to close after), is +11.4% (Nov 2024), +13.9% (Feb 2025), -4.6% (May 2025), -5.6% (Aug 2025), +0.04% (Nov 2025, despite +5.8% after hours), -3.7% (Feb 2026), -14.0% (May 2026) and -4.9% (Aug 2026). The last six prints were none up and five down. The stock now enters the print after a steady +16.6% 20-day run (23.24 on 10-14 to 27.73 on 11-10), on top of the 4.3% Flightscape pop.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line is the history itself: 0 of the last 6 prints closed up, median -4.75%. Before the Nov 2025 print the stock ran up, popped after hours and faded to flat.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is already in the price, by definition. What may not be priced is how this holder base has reacted after a run: the baseline carried no history (n=0, FPI on 6-K), so the sealed baseline gives no base rate to anchor on. Short interest is under 2%, so no squeeze mechanism offsets it.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers (2026-11-03) notes bullish sentiment up to 30.4% from 25.0% and a post-earnings range of 22.97-28.89, so spot sits near the top of that range (https://finviz.com/news/414815/caes-defense-momentum-faces-a-civil-margin-test-as-middle-east-drag-lingers). Release dates: https://www.itiger.com/news/1194683118 (Nov 2025) and https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/2026/05/22/iran-war-hammers-caes-bottom-line-with-training-centre-shutdowns-on-the-horizon/ (May 2026).

findings.finding: Civil orders in Q2: at Farnborough on 2026-07-20, inside CAE's Q2, Turkish Airlines ordered 5 full-flight simulators (2 A321neo, 2 B787, 1 A350) plus 2 A350 FTDs, with options for 2 more FFS. That one order is close to Q1's total of 6 FFS sales and supports civil book-to-bill above 1 after Q1's 1.31x, against the May narrative of 'one of the weakest order years since COVID'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders/backlog drove May 2026: civil backlog below parity 'scares the market' and the stock fell 14% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cae-inc-q4-2026-defense-grows-9-but-a-civil-backlog-below-parity-scares-the-market).
findings.why_not_priced: It was a public press release, so it is mostly priced. What is not known is whether total Q2 FFS sales and defense orders (Q1 defense book-to-bill 0.85) bring consolidated orders above 1x. Small.

findings.finding: US pilot hiring by the 13 largest carriers (FAPA) was 3,863 in the 12 months to July 2026, +74% on 2,215 a year earlier, and ALPA (October 2026) calls the pilot employment outlook strong. This supports North American training-centre utilisation (Q1 72.2% against 68.8%), which offsets part of the Gulf drag. Boeing delivered 161 jets in Q3, its most since 2018.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Utilisation recovery has not been rewarded in isolation: Q1 utilisation rose to 72.2% and the stock fell 4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public industry series, and the transmission to CAE's segment margin has not been confirmed by the company, hence small. They are filed as the offset to the bearish civil findings: the rest of the civil network, outside the Gulf, has to do well for the bar to be met.

findings.finding: A proposed C$38.25M securities class-action settlement involving CAE and former executives (reported 2026-10-02) may be booked as a provision in Q2 or Q3. It sits below adjusted operating income and is likely partly insured.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, about 0.3% of market cap and probably excluded from adjusted EPS. It is sized at a fraction because it does not touch the guide.

findings.finding: CAE USA won a $15M sole-source Air Force contract for Taiwan F-16 mission training centre support on 2026-10-28. It falls after the quarter, so it is a Q3 order, and it is tiny against about C$2.2B of annual defense revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It is immaterial; filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: The Flightscape sale (US$500M EV) closes in H1 2027, so the cash and any accretion land then. Only an announcement made in the window counts above.
The Canadian Gripen decision, for which CAE has an MOU with Saab for training and support, had no decision date as of late July 2026.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and no history, so the only market statement is the tape: a +16.6% run into the print. The negative lean agrees with selling a run on a name that has sold its last six prints, which is why it is held small rather than sized as a contrarian call.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside guidance): the Emirates/Gulf finding moved from -0.8 to -0.7, because management had already guided one or two more quarters of Middle East drag; the remaining size is the H2-assumption risk.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the consensus-arithmetic finding moved from -0.7 to -0.6; it is an inference from company documents, not a Q2 company number.
Pessimism-artefact lesson: p_up moved from 42 to 43 because six of eight findings lean negative; abs_move_pct is unchanged at 6.0 (rebuilt median 5.25 from 8 confirmed prints, mean about 7.3).
FPI history lesson: already applied before reading; the base rate was rebuilt from 8 confirmed release dates via Yahoo daily closes.
